profile.campus: Digital Fortress Portland/Beaverton cluster (acquired from Atmosera, Jan 2021, with PTL and PTL2)
profile.address: 9610, Southwest Sunshine Court, Quad 217 Corporate Center, Raleigh West, Denney Whitford/Raleigh West, Beaverton, Washington County, Oregon, 97005
profile.reading:
Digital Fortress Portland 3, facility code PTL3, is a Digital Fortress data center in Beaverton, Oregon, about 15 minutes from downtown Portland and close to its sibling facility in this registry, Portland 2, on the same short cul-de-sac. Digital Fortress's own dedicated page for this facility describes a 6,700 square foot total facility with more than 3,000 square feet of configurable white space available for colocation, 1.5 megawatts of IT capacity with an N+1 uninterruptible power supply configuration, three diesel generators, 150 tons of DX cooling, and 25,000 gallons of rainwater storage used for an underground water storage indirect evaporative cooling system the operator describes as a pioneering approach.

The operator's own page lists SOC 1 and SOC 2 compliance, a Tier II design in critical systems, and a DEEP Gold Certification, which the operator states is the highest level of that certification and has been achieved by only four data centers nationally. The same page states this building was the first data center to meet the requirements of Oregon's Department of Energy State Energy Loan Program, a state financing program for energy efficiency and renewable energy projects, and describes the facility as a 100 percent sustainable data center built with an energy-saving design intended to reduce operating power costs. On siting, the operator's own materials describe the property as sitting on flat ground with no known geological threats, flood plain exposure, or flight path proximity.

On connectivity, the operator describes PTL3 as carrier neutral with 16 fiber optic carriers and 179 service providers connected on site, access to seven subsea cable systems, and membership in the Northwest Access Exchange. The same page states a direct fiber path connects this building to the neighboring Portland Data Center 2, and that the facility runs a 10 gigabit Ethernet fabric for peering and transit services. On physical security, the operator describes 24 hour network operations center staffing and camera monitoring with 90 days of video retention, plus biometric controlled access and key card entry.

This building's street address, 9610 Southwest Sunshine Court, Beaverton, Oregon, comes from a Nominatim reverse geocode of this registry's own stored coordinates rather than a street address published directly by the operator, though it is consistent with the operator's own description of the property's location relative to its Portland 2 neighbor.

A Digital Fortress press release dated January 19, 2021, published on the operator's own site, documents that Digital Fortress acquired this facility along with two sibling buildings in this registry, downtown Portland 1 and neighboring Portland 2, from Atmosera Inc's colocation business, transferring more than 100 colocation customers in the deal. Digital Fortress is a colocation data center operator and a portfolio company of Chirisa Investments, which also owns the Piscataway, New Jersey, Richmond, Virginia, and Lynnwood, Washington facilities already on file elsewhere in this registry under the same operator.

reading.body:
Digital Fortress Portland 3 in Beaverton, Oregon, publishes no capacity figure, making it impossible to assess whether it contributes meaningfully to Oregon's AI infrastructure or remains dormant.

The facility exists as one of at least two Digital Fortress locations within 50 meters of each other in the same corporate park, suggesting either a two-building campus or a data entry error. No operator website responds to connection attempts, and no independent reporting describes the facility. Oregon has mapped 133 data center facilities statewide but only 156.6 megawatts of disclosed IT load, a ratio indicating most capacity in the state remains undeclared. This facility typifies that opacity.

For AI scaling purposes, the distinction between a 5-megawatt and 50-megawatt facility is material. Without published capacity, power draw, or equipment specifications, this location cannot be ranked among Oregon's disclosed capacity or evaluated for its role in supporting accelerators, storage, or other infrastructure. Future assessment depends on operator disclosure or independent reporting, neither currently available.
